comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official Maastricht University SBE Outline Study Programme 'Bachelor Economics and Business Economics, Specialisation Economics 2026-2027' (s0), which is based on the Bachelor Education and Examination Regulations (EER) and states the credit rules. Year 1 is common to all four specialisations: eight compulsory 6.5-EC courses (Management of Organisations and Marketing, Quantitative Methods I, Economics and Global Challenges, Accounting and Financial Reporting, Microeconomics, Quantitative Methods II, Macroeconomics, Finance) and two compulsory 4-EC skills trainings (Philosophy of Science, Economy Game) = 60 EC. Year 2 (Economics specialisation) has eight compulsory 6.5-EC courses (Microeconomics: Choices, Markets and Welfare, Quantitative Methods III, Macroeconomics and Economic Policy, Public Economics, Economic Growth and Institutions, International Trade, Labour Economics, Institutional Economics) and two elective 4-EC skills trainings = 60 EC. Year 3 comprises a 26-EC study-abroad period, three 6.5-EC electives, two compulsory 2-EC skills trainings (Global Citizenship Skills, Leadership Skills), one 2.5-EC thesis skills training (Writing a Bachelor's Thesis) and an 8-EC Bachelor's thesis = 60 EC. The outline restricts the three electives to three viable combinations of Economics, Quantitative Economics and Business electives without naming the courses, so they are preserved as restricted-choice components rather than filled with named courses; the two year-2 elective skills are likewise open elective space. The outline also offers two SPARK year-3 variants that replace the two skills trainings and the thesis skills training with a thesis proposal and a Complex Societal Challenge project; the standard variant was instantiated. The programme has four formal specialisations chosen for year 2 (Economics, Economics and Management of Information, Emerging Markets, International Business Economics; s3 to s6); the Economics specialisation was selected under the neutral broad-identity rule (see routeSelection). The 2024-2025 curriculum page (s2) lists the same structure under an older title ('International Economic Relations' for the 2026-2027 'Economics and Global Challenges') and is used for context only. The official pages name the components and their EC but do not itemise course content, and the Maastricht course catalogue could not be reached from the production environment, so comparator alignment relies on component titles, the specialisation descriptions and the stated credits; the three Quantitative Methods components are aligned only on their stated function as the programme's quantitative training. Three-year, English-language, full-time programme in Maastricht.

alternatives.concept: The strongest defensible UCR response to the Bachelor Economics and Business Economics (Economics specialisation) at Maastricht University, which combines a common year of economics, accounting, finance, management, marketing and quantitative methods with a year of core economics (micro, macro, public, growth, trade, labour and institutions) and a third year of electives, study abroad and a thesis. The programme rebuilds that core from UCR's economics track (introductory, macro, micro, public economics, econometrics and behavioural economics), the business track for accounting, finance, strategy, marketing and organisations, statistics, mathematics and data courses for the quantitative training, and politics and sociology courses for the role of the state, international relations and the sociological perspective the Economics specialisation combines with economics. It preserves genuine limitations: UCR has no labour economics, international trade, institutional economics or macroeconomic-policy course, no industrial-organisation or managerial-economics course, and no independent thesis course.

alternatives.concept: A genuinely different route built on the Emerging Markets specialisation, one of the four formal Maastricht specialisations, which studies rising economic powers and other developing economies, how culture and politics shape their business environment and how to manage responsibly in fragile economies. It keeps a smaller economic and quantitative base (macro, micro, public economics, econometrics, accounting and finance) and shifts the organising priority from the closest match's marketing, organisational, sociological-introductory and data-science content to how political institutions, geopolitics, colonial and historical context, ethics, cross-border business law and sustainability governance shape economic growth and business conduct. UCR has no development-economics, emerging-markets or international-trade course, so the programme approaches emerging markets through general economics, international business and governance, comparative politics, international relations, sociology, history, law and ethics rather than reproducing the specialisation.

Economics and business together make up about half of the programme and politics, culture and ethics the other half, so the label names the economics-and-business core and the political, cultural and responsible-business context; it does not claim an emerging-markets or development-economics programme, which UCR does not offer.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Alternative 1 organises the programme around the target's core economic and business-economics curriculum, with marketing, organisations, an introduction to sociology and applied data analysis alongside it. Alternative 2 changes the organising priority to the Emerging Markets specialisation's own commitment to how culture and politics shape the business environment and to responsible management and policy in fragile economies (registry rows 5782 and 5786 to 5789), and replaces those strands with the political, cultural, legal, ethical and governance content. The eight courses that differ from Alternative 1 (Transnational Business Law, Leadership & Diversity Management, Governance of Sustainability, History of Empires, Ethics, Qualitative Research Methodology, Modern Sociology, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory) are consequences of that concept: Transnational Business Law implements cross-border legal environments and foreign investment, Modern Sociology, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory and History of Empires supply the cultural and historical context, Ethics and Leadership & Diversity Management the responsible-management and cross-cultural strand, Governance of Sustainability the policy strand and Qualitative Research Methodology the method for studying political and cultural contexts. They replace (Business & Economy in the Age of AI, Behavioral Economics, Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Market Research, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Mathematical Methods, Probability & Statistics, Introduction to Sociology) in the closest match. The two programmes share 16 courses (the economics, finance, statistics and international core) and each has eight courses the other lacks, above the four-course floor.

alternatives.concept: A genuinely different route built on the Economics and Management of Information specialisation, which asks how companies use information technology to stay ahead of the competition, how digital technologies change competition and innovation, what information is worth and what legal, social and ethical questions IT raises. It keeps the economic core (micro, macro, public economics, behavioural economics and econometrics) and a statistical base and shifts the organising priority to information and technology: programming, databases, software development, algorithms, data science and machine learning, decision-making under uncertainty, AI ethics, digital strategy, AI and business, digital commerce law and marketing technology. UCR has no information-systems, knowledge-management or IT-law course and no information-economics course, so the programme covers the specialisation's territory through computing, data, digital-business, law and ethics courses rather than reproducing it.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Bachelor Economics and Business Economics, and the official 2026-2027 outline requires one of four formal specialisations for years 2 and 3 (Economics, Economics and Management of Information, Emerging Markets, International Business Economics), so one must be instantiated. Year 1 is common to all four and consists of general economics, accounting, finance, management, marketing and quantitative methods. The Economics specialisation is the one that continues the programme's own name and its general economic-analysis identity: its second-year core is microeconomic, macroeconomic, public, growth, trade, labour and institutional economics, and the specialisation page describes it as giving insight into global markets and the role of the state and as mastering tools to analyse economic policy and growth. Emerging Markets is a regional focus, Economics and Management of Information is an IT-oriented focus and International Business Economics is a firm-level focus, so each is more specialised. The Economics specialisation is also the first specialisation in the official order, which would decide the choice if the specialisations were judged equally general. The choice was made from official evidence alone and does not improve the UCR match: the year-2 economics courses on labour, trade, institutions and growth, the study-abroad period, the electives and the thesis remain without a UCR counterpart.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Foundations precede the courses that build on them wherever the schedule allows: Introduction to Economics (semester 1) precedes International Macroeconomics (3), Microeconomics & Behavior and Public Economics (4) and Econometrics and Behavioral Economics (6); Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations (1) precedes Money, Banking & Finance and Strategy & Digital Transformation (2), International Business & Governance (5) and Market Research (6); Research Methods & Statistics and Mathematical Methods (2) precede Probability & Statistics (3), Econometrics (6) and every course that formally requires them; Accounting & Corporate Finance (1) precedes Money, Banking & Finance (2); Introduction to Data Science (3) precedes the empirical work of Market Research and Econometrics (6); Statistics & Experimental Methods (3) precedes Econometrics (6). Public Economics only runs in semester 4, Business & Economy in the Age of AI only in semester 4 and International Business & Governance only in semesters 1 and 5, and they sit there. Formal prerequisites are all satisfied and every course sits in a semester in which it is offered. Personal & Professional Development is in year 1.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three UCR alternatives are defensible and the maximum was reached. Alternative 1 owns fourteen generator-eligible rows that describe the Economics specialisation's own core (5772 to 5776, 5779, 5781, 5783, 5790 to 5794 and 5802): how economies and businesses work, global challenges, microeconomics, macroeconomics, management and strategy, finance, quantitative economic analysis, consumer behaviour, wage inequality, ageing and public budgets, financial crises, the role of the state and independent research. It is the closest feasible response, but UCR has no labour-economics, international-trade, institutional-economics or macroeconomic-policy course. Three further candidate directions from the other three formal specialisations were assessed. Emerging markets (rows 5782, 5786 to 5789, supported by 5780) passed evidence, coherence, distinctness and feasibility and became Alternative 2: the rows are stable study directions naming culture, politics, responsible management and business opportunities in rising economies, and UCR offers comparative politics, international relations, sociology, history, ethics, cross-border business law and sustainability governance; it shares 16 courses with Alternative 1 and differs in 8. Economics and management of information (rows 5784, 5795, 5797 and 5798, supported by 5796) passed all four gates and became Alternative 3: UCR offers programming, databases, software development, data science, machine learning, AI ethics, digital strategy and digital-commerce law; it shares 15 courses with Alternative 1 and 12 with Alternative 2. International business economics (rows 5785, 5799, 5800 and 5801) was rejected as not substantively distinct: UCR has one international business course (International Business & Governance) and its finance, strategy, accounting and trade-related content is already carried by the closest match and by Alternative 2, so a further concept would only re-sort those courses and would share more than 20 of its 24 courses with one of them. Every generator-eligible row is either covered by the closest-match core or assigned to one candidate; the remaining rows are support-only curricular topics (5777, 5778, 5780 and 5796) or search-only outcome rows (5803 to 5806) and cannot generate a direction. All three included alternatives passed the 30-EC pairwise floor and mechanical feasibility against the enriched workbook.

notes.text: Both programmes include substantial study of economic theory, public economics, finance and quantitative methods. The Bachelor Economics and Business Economics (Economics specialisation) additionally includes specialist work in labour economics, international trade, institutional economics, economic growth and macroeconomic policy. UCR students can instead combine economics, business, statistics, politics and sociology courses, but those specialist components are not offered at the same level of depth.

The Bachelor Economics and Business Economics organises study around a common first year, a second-year specialisation and a third year of study abroad, electives and a thesis. At UCR, comparable subjects are distributed across courses in economics, business, quantitative methods, politics and sociology. The UCR programmes therefore cover related territory through a different curricular structure rather than reproducing the target course by course.
